text: The pig respiratory tract structure includes: nostrils, the entry point for air into the nasal passage; turbinate bones, four thin curling bones in the pig's nose; the larynx and tonsil at the back of the mouth; the trachea in the neck, which passes down into the chest and divides into two bronchi in the lungs; and lungs with 7 lobes, spongy and soft in texture. The bronchi branch into progressively smaller bronchi, becoming bronchioles that terminate in tiny air sacs called alveoli. The respiratory tract is lined by a mucous membrane, so called because it is bathed in sticky mucus.
